messages:
tim_sre: Heads-up — seeing provisioning failures in eu-west1. ~25% of new GPU nodes fail with 'nvlink init timeout'. Affected pool: rw-eu-gpu-pool-4. Customers pinned to eu-west1 seeing higher queue and token latency. Raising an incident.

cheng_oncall: On it. Any recent image/kernel changes or infra rollouts in eu-west1?

maria_ops: I'll draft a status page entry once we have scope. Tentative wording: 'Partial degradation in eu-west1 affecting provisioning and increased latency for some customers. Engineers are investigating and shifting traffic where possible.'

devon_infra: Autoscaler tried 3x to replace nodes and hit backoff due to repeated init failures. Putting pool in manual drain to avoid oscillation.

ops-bot: autoscaler-event: rw-eu-gpu-pool-4 attempted_scale_up=6 failed_inits=14 backoff=true

tim_sre: Quick mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic off eu-west1 where routing policy allows, 2) prevent further automatic scale-ups on the affected pool, 3) prioritize reserved/dedicated pools for enterprise fleets, 4) start root-cause investigation on nvlink/init path.

cheng_oncall: Agreed. I'll start moving _unpinned_ traffic. Running a staged traffic shift to avoid overloading fallback regions.

devon_infra: Command I'll run (dry-run first):
```
# shift 60% of unpinned traffic from eu-west1 -> eu-central1
rbctl route set-weight --from eu-west1 --to eu-central1 --pct 60 --dry-run=true
```

tim_sre: After dry-run checks, flip to live. Also disable scale-up for rw-eu-gpu-pool-4:
```
rbctl pool update rw-eu-gpu-pool-4 --autoscale=off --reason="init failures"
```

maria_ops: Draft statuspage (v1):
"We are experiencing partial provisioning failures in eu-west1 which may cause increased latency or failed requests for some customers. We are shifting traffic to healthy regions and provisioning replacement nodes. Our engineers are investigating the cause and will post updates every 30 minutes. Current ETA for full recovery: ~90 minutes."

support_alan: I'll open P1 cases for affected enterprise customers and send the draft status message to legal/comms for a quick review. Tagging priority customers: @AcmeCorp @NovaAI @BrightChat (we have direct SLA contacts).

tim_sre: Initial investigation shows a driver/firmware regression on nodes booting with nvidia-driver 525.33.x — nodes with older driver versions boot fine. Suspecting recent node image change in the EU image build cluster.

devon_infra: Rolling back the image build pipeline to previous driver (525.22) for new nodes. Patch/deploy to image builder in progress.

ops-bot: image-build: rollback-triggered id=imgb-2026-04-12-007 by devon_infra

cheng_oncall: I'm monitoring provisioning logs. After forcing the older driver on a test node, init succeeds. Starting controlled repro: bring up 5 test nodes with 525.22.

tim_sre: If tests pass, we can resume safe provisioning and gradually route traffic back. Do NOT re-enable autoscale on pool until confirmed.

statusbot: Incident created: INC-2026-3323 — Partial degradation in eu-west1. Statuspage updated (incident).

maria_ops: Posted initial status (v1) on status.redwood.ai and created the incident page. Will send first customer-facing email in 10m.

devon_infra: Test node results: 4/5 boots OK with 525.22, one failed due to unrelated disk mount issue. New nodes provisioning success rate improved to ~80%.

tim_sre: Good. Start a slow enable: change traffic shift to 40% back once provision rate hits >90% for 10 mins. We'll keep enterprise reservations at top priority for replacement nodes.

cheng_oncall: Implementing progressive traffic reweighting now.

maria_ops: Status update (v2) drafted: 'Update 30m — provisioning success rate improving after image rollback. We have shifted traffic and prioritized reserved pools. Next update in 30m or sooner. ETA revised to ~45 minutes.' Posting now.

support_alan: Sent targeted emails to enterprise contacts and opened support tickets with the engineering runbook attached.

tim_sre: Next steps: continue repro and full verification, monitor autoscaler logs for regressions, coordinate with cloud vendor if nvlink errors persist.

maria_ops: Posting final update for this thread: statuspage updated, customers notified. Closing internal incident thread here; we'll reopen if error rates climb again. :thumbsup:
